name: GPT-4.1
description: A three-model API family introduced together across capability, latency, and cost tiers.

name: GPT-5.6
description: The current GPT-5 generation, released for general availability on 2026-07-09 after a limited preview of its flagship tier. In OpenAI's words the family spans three durable capability tiers: Sol (the flagship), Terra (a lower-cost model competitive with GPT-5.5), and Luna (the fastest and most affordable), where the number identifies the generation and the tier names can advance on their own cadence. It succeeds GPT-5.5.

name: GPT-5.5
description: The GPT-5 generation immediately preceding GPT-5.6, introduced in the API on 2026-04-23 as a frontier model for complex coding, research, and data-analysis work. OpenAI's GPT-5.6 documentation positions the Terra tier as competitive with GPT-5.5, and its model documentation still lists GPT-5.5 as available; GPT-5.6 is its successor generation.

name: GPT-5.4
description: An earlier GPT-5 generation, introduced on 2026-03-05 as OpenAI's frontier model for professional work, with state-of-the-art coding, computer use, and a roughly one-million-token context window. It precedes GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6 in the GPT-5 line.

name: GPT-5
description: The first GPT-5 generation and the root of the line that GPT-5.4, GPT-5.5, and GPT-5.6 build on. Its date is taken from the pinned API snapshot gpt-5-2025-08-07; OpenAI's model documentation now labels GPT-5 a previous model and recommends GPT-5.6 in its place.

name: Claude 5
description: The current Claude generation. Fable and Mythos share the same capabilities and specifications, but Fable is widely released while Mythos is restricted to approved customers. Opus is the tier Anthropic recommends for complex coding work that runs over many steps.

name: Claude 4.5
description: The 2025 Claude generation. Anthropic lists Sonnet 4.5 among legacy models while Haiku 4.5 is still documented as a current model.

name: Gemini 3
description: The current Gemini generation, spanning Pro, Flash, and Flash-Lite tiers across point releases that Google documents with individual release and shutdown dates.

name: Gemini 2.5
description: The preceding Gemini generation. Its stable Pro and Flash models remain generally available and share a single technical report.

name: Llama 4
description: Meta's first generation built to handle text and images together rather than having image support added afterwards. Each token — one of the small chunks that text and images are broken into — is handled by only a fraction of the network rather than all of it. The weights can be downloaded under a community licence.

name: Llama 3
description: Meta groups the whole Llama 3 line under History in its model collection. The recorded releases include Llama 3.1 405B, Llama 3.2 text and vision sizes, and Llama 3.3 70B; the text releases take text in and return text, while Llama 3.2 Vision takes text and images in and returns text.

name: Muse
description: Muse is Meta Superintelligence Labs' family of proprietary, hosted models spanning multimodal reasoning (Muse Spark), image generation (Muse Image), and video generation (Muse Video).

name: GPT-5.1
description: A GPT-5 generation introduced for developers on 2025-11-13 for coding and agentic tasks with configurable reasoning and non-reasoning effort.

name: GPT-5.2
description: A GPT-5 generation introduced on 2025-12-11 for professional work with reasoning, long-context understanding, coding, and vision.

name: GPT-5.3-Codex
description: A Codex-native GPT-5.3 coding family for agentic coding tasks and long-horizon technical work.

name: GPT-Image
description: OpenAI image-generation and editing models in the GPT naming line.

name: Claude 4.6
description: A 2026 Claude generation represented by Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6, with coding, computer-use, agentic, and long-context upgrades over preceding Claude 4 models.

name: Claude 4.7
description: A 2026 Claude generation represented by Opus 4.7, with advanced software-engineering, long-running-task, and higher-resolution vision improvements over Opus 4.6.

name: Claude 4.8
description: A 2026 Claude generation represented by Opus 4.8, which Anthropic says builds on Opus 4.7 with benchmark and collaboration improvements.

name: Grok 4
description: The creator’s Grok 4 generation, opened by the Grok 4 announcement of 9 July 2025 and continued by the 4.5 and 4.6 point releases. Every member is offered through the creator’s hosted API only, and the creator publishes no parameter count for any of them. The 4.5 documentation lists grok-build-latest as an alias of that model, which is a different thing from the grok-build-0.1 model listed on the same pricing page. Grok 4 itself is not recorded as a release here: its announcement is dated, but its model documentation page is no longer served, so its modalities and context window cannot be sourced.

name: Mistral Large 3
description: The creator’s sparse mixture-of-experts generation, announced as part of Mistral 3 and released under the Apache 2.0 licence with both a hosted API and downloadable weights.

name: Ministral 3
description: The edge-oriented dense generation announced alongside Mistral Large 3 in three sizes of 3B, 8B, and 14B parameters, each published with base, instruct, and reasoning variants under the Apache 2.0 licence.

name: Devstral 2
description: The creator’s agentic software-engineering generation, published in two sizes under two different licences: the 123B model under a licence of the creator’s own drafting and the 24B model under Apache 2.0.

name: Mistral Small 4
description: A mixture-of-experts generation positioned for general-purpose use with an optional reasoning mode toggled per request, published under the Apache 2.0 licence.

name: DeepSeek-V4
description: The creator’s mixture-of-experts generation, published in a larger Pro and a smaller Flash size on the same day under the MIT licence. Both cards describe the published weights as a preview of the series.

name: DeepSeek-V3.2
description: The generation preceding DeepSeek-V4, published under the MIT licence and described by its card as introducing DeepSeek Sparse Attention for long-context work.

name: Qwen3.8
description: Alibaba Cloud’s Qwen3.8 generation, published as downloadable weights on Hugging Face Hub and ModelScope: a sparse mixture-of-experts flagship alongside a dense vision-language model. Qwen is the family; the clouds that offer it, including Amazon’s, are separate entities recorded as serving platforms.

name: MAI
description: The in-house model line built by Microsoft AI, opened in August 2025 with MAI-Voice-1 and MAI-1-preview and catalogued by Microsoft AI as foundational models across reasoning, coding, image, voice and transcription. These are models Microsoft created. Microsoft Copilot, the product some of them are placed inside, and Microsoft Foundry, the platform they are served on, are recorded separately and are not part of this family.

name: Fara
description: Microsoft Research AI Frontiers’ line of computer-use agent models for web browsers, published with downloadable weights under the MIT licence. It is a different line from the MAI models Microsoft AI builds: the same creator company, a different team, and separate evidence. Its models are fine-tuned from open-weight base models created by other organizations, which changes nothing about who created the Fara models themselves.

name: Amazon Nova 2
description: Amazon’s second generation of Nova foundation models, announced by AWS in December 2025 as "our next generation of general models" and built, per Amazon, on technologies originally developed for Amazon’s own applications. Nova is a family Amazon created; Amazon Bedrock, where it is served alongside hundreds of other companies’ models, is a serving platform and is recorded separately.

name: Command A
description: Cohere's Command A line of enterprise text-generation models. Cohere names the grouping and places Command A+ inside it — "Command A+ offers the last model in the Command A family" — and its launch post compares Command A+ "with other models in the Command A family". Cohere separately describes a wider Command family that also takes in the Command R models; that broader grouping is not this family. The first release date is the month carried by the earliest member Cohere lists, command-a-03-2025, and is recorded at month precision because no approved source states a day.

name: OLMo 2
description: AI2’s second-generation fully open OLMo language models, released with open weights, data, and training code.

name: Falcon-H1
description: TII’s Falcon-H1 series of hybrid attention–state-space language models, released as open weights.

name: Nemotron-4 340B
description: NVIDIA’s Nemotron-4 340B family of open-weight base, instruct, and reward models aimed at synthetic data generation.

name: Jamba
description: AI21 Labs’ Jamba family of hybrid Mamba–Transformer (SSM) language models with long context support.

name: GLM-4.5
description: Zhipu AI’s GLM-4.5 series of Mixture-of-Experts foundation models unifying reasoning, coding, and agent capabilities.

name: Kimi K2
description: Moonshot AI’s Kimi K2 family of trillion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts language models built for agentic and coding tasks.

name: Pythia
description: EleutherAI’s Pythia scaling suite, a set of language models trained on the same data in the same order across eight sizes, published with per-step checkpoints so that training behaviour can be studied.

name: EXAONE 3.5
description: LG AI Research’s EXAONE 3.5 series of instruction-tuned bilingual English and Korean language models, released at 2.4B, 7.8B, and 32B sizes with a 32,768-token context length.

name: EXAONE 4.0
description: LG AI Research’s EXAONE 4.0 series, which integrates a non-reasoning mode and a reasoning mode in one model and extends the series' language coverage to Spanish alongside English and Korean. The series consists of two sizes: a mid-size 32B model and a small-size 1.2B model.

name: Arctic
description: Snowflake’s Arctic family of dense-MoE hybrid language models, combining a dense transformer with a residual Mixture-of-Experts MLP and published under Apache-2.0.

name: Solar Pro
description: Upstage’s Solar Pro line, built by depth up-scaling a smaller model into a larger one and intended to run on a single GPU. Only the preview release is recorded here, because it is the only member the sources describe as published.

name: Granite 4.2
description: IBM’s Granite 4.2 generation: dense, decoder-only reasoning models in 3B, 8B and 30B, each with a thinking / non-thinking switch and native tool calling, released under the Apache 2.0 licence. Only the 30B release is recorded here.

name: ERNIE 4.5
description: Baidu’s ERNIE 4.5 generation, which its repository describes as a family of large-scale multimodal models in ten variants spanning text and vision-language mixture-of-experts models, all published under Apache 2.0. Only the 300B text model is recorded here.

name: HunyuanVideo
description: Tencent’s open-weight video generation line within the Hunyuan model family, published with inference code and weights under Tencent’s own community licence.

name: Seed-OSS
description: ByteDance Seed’s open-source language model series, released in base and instruction-tuned 36B forms under Apache 2.0 with a long context length.

name: Stable Diffusion 3.5
description: Stability AI’s Stable Diffusion 3.5 generation of text-to-image diffusion transformers, published under the Stability AI Community License. Only the Large model is recorded here.

name: DBRX
description: Databricks’ mixture-of-experts language model, published as base and instruction-tuned weights under the Databricks Open Model License and served to Databricks customers through APIs.

name: MiniMax-M1
description: MiniMax’s M1 series of open-weight hybrid Mixture-of-Experts reasoning models, combining a lightning attention mechanism with a natively supported context length of 1 million tokens, published in two thinking-budget versions.

name: OpenELM
description: Apple’s family of open efficient language models, released in pretrained and instruction-tuned form at 270M, 450M, 1.1B and 3B parameters under a licence limiting them to scientific research.

name: SmolLM3
description: Hugging Face’s own small language model line, published as a fully open 3B model with dual-mode reasoning and long-context support.

name: Yi-1.5
description: 01.AI’s upgraded Yi series, continuously pre-trained on Yi with a further 500B-token corpus and fine-tuned on 3M samples, distributed under the Apache 2.0 licence.

name: MiniMax-Text-01
description: MiniMax’s text-only mixture-of-experts language model line, with 456 billion total parameters and 45.9 billion activated per token, published as downloadable weights under the MiniMax Model License.

name: EvoLLM-JP
description: Sakana AI’s experimental general-purpose Japanese language model, produced by merging existing models with its Evolutionary Model Merge method and released as a research prototype.

name: Sarvam-M
description: Sarvam AI’s multilingual hybrid-reasoning language model, post-trained from Mistral Small on Indian languages alongside English.

name: HyperCLOVA X SEED
description: NAVER’s line of lightweight HyperCLOVA X models, announced as three models — 3B, 1.5B and 0.5B — released as open source and free for commercial use. The announcement describes the 3B sibling as a vision-language model; only the 1.5B text model is recorded as a release here, so the family carries only that release’s category rather than claiming a modality no recorded release covers.

name: Pharia-1-LLM
description: Aleph Alpha's Pharia-1 foundation model family, announced as "our new foundation model family that includes Pharia-1-LLM-7B-control and Pharia-1-LLM-7B-control-aligned". The 7B control model is recorded here; it is culturally and linguistically optimized for German, French and Spanish.

name: Reka Flash
description: Reka AI's Reka Flash line of compact reasoning models. Reka Flash 3.1, recorded here, is described by Reka as "an update to our Reka Flash 3" that "is particularly strong on coding and as a base model to be finetuned on agentic tasks".

name: Hermes 4
description: Nous Research's Hermes 4 generation of steerable, hybrid-mode reasoning models. The 14B member recorded here is described on its card as "a frontier, hybrid-mode reasoning model based on Qwen 3 14B by Nous Research".

name: LFM2
description: Liquid AI's second series of Liquid Foundation Models, built for on-device inference on a hybrid architecture of "10 double-gated short-range convolution blocks and 6 blocks of grouped query attention". Three dense checkpoints were released at 0.35B, 0.7B and 1.2B parameters; the 1.2B model is recorded here.

name: MiMo-7B
description: Xiaomi's MiMo-7B series, "a series of models trained from scratch and born for reasoning tasks", spanning base, SFT and RL checkpoints. The RL checkpoint MiMo-7B-RL-0530 is recorded here.

name: SEA-LION v3
description: AI Singapore's third SEA-LION generation, "a collection of 3 models (and their variants)" for Southeast-Asian languages, "released in Dec 2024". The Llama-based 8B model is recorded here.

name: Yi
description: 01.AI’s original Yi series, opened on 2023-11-02 with bilingual English/Chinese base models at 6B and 34B, extended three days later with 200K-context base models and on 2023-11-23 with chat models, and later with 9B and vision-language members. It is the series the Yi-1.5 generation was continuously pre-trained from.

name: Qwen3.5
description: Alibaba Cloud’s Qwen3.5 generation, announced on 2026-02-16 with a 397B-A17B mixture-of-experts flagship and extended over the following fortnight with 122B-A10B, 35B-A3B and 27B variants and then a set of smaller ones, all published as downloadable weights on Hugging Face Hub and ModelScope. A Qwen generation is the family. Qwen3.5-Plus, which the flagship’s card describes as the hosted version corresponding to these weights, is a separate artefact and is not recorded here.

name: Qwen3.6
description: Alibaba Cloud’s Qwen3.6 generation, whose first open-weight variant reached Hugging Face Hub and ModelScope on 2026-04-16 and was followed by a dense 27B variant on 2026-04-22. Its card presents the generation as a successor to Qwen3.5 focused on agentic coding and on retaining reasoning context between turns.

name: GPT-Neo
description: EleutherAI’s GPT-Neo class of autoregressive language models, trained on the Pile as an open replication of the GPT-3 architecture. The repository’s dated release note announces "two pretrained GPT-Neo models" under the heading "Update 21/03/2021", which is what the first release date records, and the two checkpoints it links are the 1.3B and the 2.7B. The status is recorded as unknown: no source consulted states a lifecycle for the GPT-Neo weights. The README does say the GPT-Neo training *code* is no longer maintained, which is a statement about the code and not about the published models, so it is deliberately not read as a family status.

name: Granite 4.0
description: IBM’s Granite 4.0 generation of enterprise language models, which IBM describes as a collection comprising "multiple model sizes and architecture styles" — the hybrid Mamba/transformer H-Small, H-Tiny and H-Micro, plus a conventional-attention Micro. The first release date is 2 October 2025, the date the Granite 4.0 model cards state for themselves under "Release Date"; IBM’s launch post carries the same date only as a publication dateline, which is not what this record rests on. The status is recorded as unknown: IBM states no lifecycle for the generation, and a newer Granite 4.2 is separately recorded in this dataset, so "current" would be an inference rather than a sourced fact.

name: Falcon 180B
description: TII's 180-billion-parameter causal decoder-only language model, trained on 3.5 trillion tokens of RefinedWeb and released under the Falcon 180B TII License. A distinct earlier family from the hybrid-architecture Falcon-H1.

name: Molmo
description: Ai2's family of open vision-language models, trained on the PixMo image-text data and distinct from the text-only OLMo family. Released with Apache-2.0 weights.
